CARDIO CLINICAL DATA INDEX — SIXTH REVISION

24 authentic recordings; 373,400 calibrated channel samples.
17 twelve-lead examples plus seven original two-channel excerpts.
Durations: 6.6–14 seconds. Each source retains its native sampling rate.
The waveform exports apply source ADC gain/baseline calibration and serialize
millivolt samples as JSON. No additional filtering, resampling, normalization,
synthetic channels or generated clinical waveforms are included.

1. clinical-ecgs.json
   Eight PTB-XL v1.0.3 records: 100 Hz, 10 seconds, 12 leads each.
   96,000 samples. Source: Wagner et al., PhysioNet.
   License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
   https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/
   https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6

2. clinical-extra.json
   Six additional PTB-XL v1.0.3 records: 100 Hz, 10 seconds, 12 leads each.
   72,000 samples. Same source and CC BY 4.0 license as above.
   Import evidence and source qualifications: clinical-extra-provenance.json.
   Together the two PTB-XL files contain 14 records and 168,000 samples.
   PTB-XL exports retain source recording-level diagnoses; added waveform
   timing landmarks are explicitly approximate teaching annotations.

3. clinical-mobitz2.json
   MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database v1.0.0 record 231: first 10 seconds,
   360 Hz, original MLII/V1 channels; 7,200 samples.
   Source: George Moody and Roger Mark, PhysioNet.
   License: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0 (ODC-By).
   https://physionet.org/content/mitdb/1.0.0/
   https://physionet.org/content/mitdb/view-license/1.0.0/
   Source identifies Mobitz II with RBBB. Original ventricular annotations
   are retained; added P-onset estimates are for animation only.
   Full attribution, changes and integrity checks:
   clinical-mobitz2-README.md and clinical-mobitz2-provenance.json.

4. clinical-stemi.json
   Three 500 Hz, 12-lead STEMI examples; 159,600 samples in total.

   ACS00004 and ACS18206: 10 seconds each; 120,000 samples.
   Source: Du et al., ACS dataset on Figshare.
   License: Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0).
   https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.29925314
   https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-026-07278-0
   Source STEMI/culprit-vessel metadata retained. QRS extrema are manually
   checked teaching landmarks; atrial timing is prescribed. Archive-entry
   CRC checks verify source bytes; inconsistent source header checksum
   fields are not claimed to pass WFDB checksums.

   LUDB record 21: source seconds 1.6–8.2, 6.6 seconds; 39,600 samples.
   Source: Kalyakulina et al., Lobachevsky University Electrocardiography
   Database v1.0.1, PhysioNet.
   License: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0 (ODC-By).
   https://physionet.org/content/ludb/1.0.1/
   https://physionet.org/content/ludb/view-license/1.0.1/
   Original clinician P/QRS fiducials are retained for included complexes.
   Source anterior/lateral/septal/apical STEMI, left anterior hemiblock and
   left-axis findings are retained as a combined presentation.
   See clinical-stemi-provenance.json, STEMI-DATA-SOURCES.txt and
   LUDB-LICENSE.txt for complete attribution, original URLs, calibration,
   hashes, cropping, timing limitations and license details.

5. clinical-tachyarrhythmias.json
   Five original two-channel, 10-second examples; 31,600 channel samples.

   MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database v1.0.0: records 202, 222 and 209,
   native 360 Hz, MLII/V1; 21,600 samples in total.
   Record 202, 1264–1274 s: source AFIB, calculated mean 123.838 bpm.
   "Rapid ventricular response" describes that measured rate; it is not
   a separate source diagnostic annotation.
   Record 222, 1690–1700 s: source AFL, mean ventricular rate 101.887 bpm.
   Record 209, 560–570 s: source SVTA, mean ventricular rate 159.669 bpm.
   The 20, 17 and 26 source QRS event markers, respectively, are retained.
   They are not exact QRS-onset fiducials. No measured atrial clock, exact
   flutter circuit, conduction ratio, AVNRT or AVRT diagnosis is added.
   Source: George Moody and Roger Mark, PhysioNet; ODC-By 1.0.
   https://physionet.org/content/mitdb/1.0.0/
   https://physionet.org/content/mitdb/view-license/1.0.0/

   MIT-BIH Malignant Ventricular Ectopy Database v1.0.0: records 421
   and 422, native 250 Hz, ECG1/ECG2; 10,000 samples in total.
   Record 421, 1360–1370 s: source VT, within a 150.232-second episode.
   Approximately 245.592 bpm is estimated from 40 visually reviewed
   ECG2 waveform maxima. The source supplies rhythm changes, not beat
   annotations; no monomorphic/polymorphic subtype is assigned.
   Record 422, 1550–1560 s: source VFIB. No discrete QRS markers or
   organized ventricular rate are assigned.
   Source: Paul Albrecht, George Moody and Roger Mark, PhysioNet.
   License: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0 (ODC-By).
   https://physionet.org/content/vfdb/1.0.0/
   https://physionet.org/content/vfdb/view-license/1.0.0/
   https://physionet.org/files/vfdb/1.0.0/annotations.shtml
   Dataset DOI: 10.13026/C22P44.

   Each crop lies wholly within its original rhythm annotation interval.
   Mean rates use 60 × (N − 1) / (last marker time − first marker time).
   Full source hashes, WFDB checksums, initial samples, exact inverse
   calibration, crop coordinates and timing status are retained in
   clinical-tachyarrhythmias-provenance.json. See the matching README
   and TACHYARRHYTHMIA-DATA-SOURCES.txt for attribution and limitations.
   Reproducible importer: scripts/import_tachyarrhythmias.py.

6. clinical-torsades.json
   Sudden Cardiac Death Holter Database v1.0.0 record 47: native 250 Hz,
   two original channels, 14 seconds; 7,000 channel samples.
   Source elapsed 06:13:10–06:13:24; header-based clock 18:13:10–18:13:24.
   Source samples 5,597,500 through 5,600,999 inclusive.
   Source: Scott Greenwald, PhysioNet; ODC-By 1.0.
   https://physionet.org/content/sddb/1.0.0/
   https://physionet.org/content/sddb/view-license/1.0.0/
   Dataset DOI: 10.13026/C2W306.

   Lerma et al. (2007), Table 1 and Figure 2, identify this source record
   as torsades de pointes in a prolonged-QT context.
   https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jelectrocard.2006.04.011
   https://www.mcgill.ca/physiological-dynamics/files/physiological-dynamics/rule_2007.pdf
   The crop contains about eight seconds of preceding complex ventricular
   ectopy/runs and six seconds in the graphically matched TdP region.
   The display transition at eight seconds has about one second of
   uncertainty and is not a validated onset fiducial. Published preceding-
   rhythm QTc context is not a QT measurement from this tachycardia strip.
   Source .ari annotations are unaudited; no reliable beat markers or
   clinical rate are assigned. No VF transition or termination is labeled.
   The paper is cited; its figure is not redistributed or digitized.

   Official source hashes, complete channel checksums, initial samples,
   exact inverse calibration, crop and diagnostic/alignment evidence:
   clinical-torsades-provenance.json and clinical-torsades-README.md.
   Attribution and license notes: TORSADES-DATA-SOURCES.txt.
   Reproducible standard-library importer: scripts/import_torsades.py.

Both generic source channels named ECG are displayed as ECG1 and ECG2
solely to distinguish their original order. Their anatomical lead axes
are unknown. Modified MLII also lacks exact electrode coordinates. No
standard lead axis or missing channel is inferred for these signals.

All adjacent 3D activation/contraction is an explanatory reference model,
not measured patient mechanics. Source beat timing, estimated VT landmarks
and schematic TdP/VF timing are explicitly distinguished. The stationary
traces support paused click/drag seeking; previous/next-beat controls are
disabled for TdP and VF because discrete beat markers are unavailable.
The opening ideal ECG and Sandbox signals are separately identified
original simulations and are excluded from these clinical totals. The
five simulated catalog examples from the fourth revision are no longer
included in Module 5; the new fast rhythms are not transferred into the
Sandbox's different mechanism model. These data checks do not assert
completion of sixth-revision browser QA.
